newsitem.title: UK: British bank urges joint action on landmines trade.
newsitem.headline: British bank urges joint action on landmines trade.

text.p: A British commercial bank on Wednesday urged its rivals to unite and help end worldwide funding for the production and sale of landmines.
The unusual call was made by Terry Thomas, managing director of the Co-Operative Bank Plc. His bank is among the leaders of the ethical investment movement in Britain.

In a letter to competitors, Thomas said a worldwide ban on landmines could be accelerated if every bank agreed never to finance the manufacture, production, stockpiling or trade in anti-personnel mines.
Banks could control letters of credit, inspect export credit guarantee certificates and monitor offshore and overseas branches, he added.

"I am a great believer that banks can be a force for good and that together we can help eradicate this despicable trade which has left a legacy of 110 million active mines in 64 countries around the world with another 100 million stockpiled waiting to be laid," he said.

The bank sparked controversy earlier this year with an advertisement claiming that "certain banks" used hundreds of millions of pounds of their customers' money to finance the supply of arms to both Iran and Iraq.

A U.N.-sponsored conference in Geneva agreed to limit the use of some landmines in May but stopped short of a ban because some countries argue they should remain a legitimate form of military defence.
